# Named paths are sealed from their plaintext whatever their state, so a stale
# secret can be kept without `--all` resealing (and churning) every object.

sesam-repo admin base.txt changed.txt

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt u
exec sesam add s t u --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add s t u'

exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s t'
exec git checkout master

# Hookless pull: s and t are stale now.
exec sesam hook uninstall
exec git merge topic
exec sesam status
stdout '2 stale'

# Naming s seals it; t stays stale and is named, u is not touched.
exec sesam seal s
stderr 'stale secrets? were not sealed because they are newer than what is revealed'
stderr 'git pull. without sesam.s hooks installed'
stderr 'sesam:   t'
stderr 'sesam seal <path>'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'BASE'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/t.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec git diff --quiet -- .sesam/objects/u.sesam

# --force-stale takes the rest.
exec sesam seal --force-stale
! stderr 'not sealed'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/t.sesam
stdout 'BASE'
exec git diff --quiet -- .sesam/objects/u.sesam

# Paths that cannot be sealed are refused, not silently preserved.
! exec sesam seal nope
stderr 'nope: not a tracked secret'
rm u
! exec sesam seal u
stderr 'u: no plaintext to seal'

-- base.txt --
BASE
-- changed.txt --
CHANGED
